Meet your driver at Tocumen International Airport and transfer to Panama City.

Check in at your chosen hotel. The rest of the day is free.
Panama City skyline with a spiral tower and city lights at dusk, Panama
Panama City: illuminated high-rises and a green spiral tower at dusk

Breakfast at the hotel. Departure at 08:00.

Spanish conquistadors founded Panama City in the 16th century. It became the first Spanish city and port on the Pacific coast. Your introduction to the capital begins in its two historic areas: Old Panama, known as Panamá Viejo, and New Panama.

In Old Panama you’ll see the surviving ruins of early 17th-century cathedrals, convents and bridges. In the newer part of the city, you’ll visit Casco Antiguo, a well-preserved colonial district and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The sightseeing tour lasts six hours. It includes the Panamá Viejo Archaeological Park and its museum, historic and modern neighbourhoods, and the former Panama Canal residential zone, where Americans who helped build the canal once lived.

Drive along Balboa Avenue beside Panama Bay, then continue on foot through the narrow streets, squares and parks of Casco Antiguo, where much of the country’s history is preserved.

The route takes you past the National Theatre, a striking example of neoclassical architecture in Panama. Visit Plaza de Francia and the Church of San José, where you’ll learn the story of its Golden Altar. You can also see the Nativity scene installed at Christmas in 2017.

Plaza Bolívar features a monument to Simón Bolívar, a national hero in many Central and South American countries. Continue to Cathedral Square, home to the Metropolitan Cathedral, which reopened after restoration in 2019, the Panama Canal Museum and the Municipal Palace.

Finish at the Amador Causeway, where there were once three separate islands: Naos, Perico and Flamenco.
